newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian law review backs cross-dressers, pigeons.
newsitem.headline: Australian law review backs cross-dressers, pigeons.

text.p: Men should be able to dress as women and walk the streets of the Australian island state of Tasmania without fear of arrest, according to a review of the island's 60-year-old police laws released on Monday.
A report by the Tasmanian Law Reform Commission on the Police Offences Act of 1935 has also recommended fortune tellers and beggars be able to operate unhindered.
But throwing nightsoil into a river or injuring a homing pigeon will remain offences under environmental and animal welfare legislation, said Don Chalmers, author of the report.
"It's a mish-mash of offences derived from English legislation of the last century, some of it framed in very archaic language, and new offences added since 1935," said Chalmers of the existing laws.
"One of the more humorous examples was the offence of being a man going around town in women's clothing during the hours of darkness," Chalmers told reporters.
Chalmers' report also recommends the repeal of offences such as wandering abroad, fortune telling, soliciting alms, loitering with reputed thieves and rescuing an impounded animal.

The report said scrutiny should also be given to laws banning the singing of profane or indecent songs in public, nude bathing and the provision of indoor public entertainment on Good Friday or Christmas Day.
A spokesman for Police Minister John Beswick said it would take up to three months to frame any new legislation recommended by the report.
